I'm not super literate on global warming - I'm more of a physics and materials science guy - so I won't dig around for facts or figures.

Instead, let me argue from an inside look at scientific culture: Scientists love to point out when others among them are wrong.

There's a big problem right now with shit-level reports being written by undergrads trying to make a name for themselves, but the real big reports (like the LIGO announcement) are fact-checked and doublechecked to death because no scientist wants to be publicly corrected. It's embarrassing, and the community loves to gossip about shit like that.

So my argument is, if it's at all possible for the current global warming theory to be wrong, how could that error possibly survive the withering gaze of a community that drools at the idea of pointing out someone being wrong?

The only real response I've heard to this is "Well the entire scientific community is conspiring together on it" but that's laughable. If we have scientists willing to advocate for young-Earth creationism, we certainly can't have a community-wide conspiracy.

There are hundreds of examples of the entire scientific community being collectively wrong on multiple topic that were published after decades of peer review.

  • Everyone agreed The coelacanths were said to be extinct for over a hundred years.

  • For decades the collective professionals of planetary research denied water was on mars, let alone that there could ever be liquid water on it.
